The core task of a NeRF network architecture is to learn a continuous volumetric scene representation $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the spatial position, $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is the volume density, and $\mathbf{c}$ is the view-dependent color.
The rendering process integrates these outputs along rays using standard volume rendering equations.

FlipNeRF is a regularization method for few-shot novel view synthesis that generates auxiliary "flipped reflection rays" from original input rays and estimated surface normals to improve rendering quality and surface normal accuracy with sparse inputs [12967-flipnerf.md].

Unlike existing regularization methods that focus on accurate depth estimation or pre-training methods requiring large datasets, FlipNeRF is optimized per scene without pre-training and derives rays from estimated normals without heuristic factors [12967-flipnerf.md].
It sets itself apart from Ref-NeRF by generating additional training rays rather than reparameterizing the radiance field's input viewing direction [12967-flipnerf.md].
